reasons: No tests are visible in this packet.
Error and not-configured states are handled on screen.
Source checks depend on exact project name matching.
An import sits in the middle of the file.

terms.meaning: A summary written by an AI model from the project data, grouped into themes.
A saved copy of an earlier answer, so the same request does not have to run again.
A request for data that the app keeps track of, remembers, and can refresh.
A short one-line banner that summarises a column.
A link from a claim to the project record and quote that support it.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the synthesis slide
sections.what: Brings in colours, the shared slide frame, house tags, the data fetch tool, icons, citation helpers, the synthesis API call, and the data types.
sections.why: These are the pieces the slide needs to show text, fetch the AI answer and open source drawers.

sections.name: BulletSources (part 1)
sections.title: Source buttons on each bullet
sections.what: Shows a small button marked with the source count, or no src when there is none. Opening it lists each source with its quote. With no sources, it says the claim is unsupported and offers the named project's stored cause fields as things to check, clearly not as proof.
sections.why: The comments say claims must be marked honestly, so a bullet without a source is labelled as such.
sections.watch_out: Check options appear only when the stored field has a source link, so a field with a value but no link is not offered.

sections.name: BulletSources (part 2)
sections.title: Slide purpose and colour setup
sections.what: A long comment explains the slide's rules: the AI only sorts the selected projects, every figure comes from the scan data, and missing causes say no cause stated. Short names then set the header colour, the chevron colour, the red for wrong and the green for right.
sections.why: The comment records the no-fabrication contract, which is the main design rule for this slide.

sections.name: ColumnHeader
sections.title: Column heading with plus or minus marker
sections.what: Draws the heading for one column: a round marker (minus for wrong, plus for right) and the words What went wrong or What went right in matching colour.
sections.why: The marker and colour make the two columns easy to tell apart at a glance.
sections.watch_out: Any side value other than negative is shown as the right-hand column, so a typo in the side name shows the wrong heading.

sections.name: CategoryBlock
sections.title: One themed group of bullets
sections.what: Shows one category name followed by its bullets. Each bullet has a marker, the bold project name, the statement text, and the source button. The project is found by matching its name in lower case without spaces at the edges.
sections.why: Groups related bullets under a theme so the column reads as a short argument.
sections.watch_out: Matching uses the exact name, so if the AI writes a project name slightly differently, its source checks are lost.

sections.name: ChevronStrap
sections.title: Coloured arrow banner
sections.what: Draws a solid coloured banner with one line of text and a pointed end. The left banner points right and the right banner points left, so they face each other under the two columns.
sections.why: Gives each column a bold closing summary line.
sections.watch_out: Long straplines wrap inside the coloured box and can make the banner tall.

sections.name: SynthesisSlide (part 1)
sections.title: Data setup, loading and regenerate
sections.what: Collects the selected project ids, requests the synthesis, and remembers the result in the browser for good. Pressing Regenerate changes the request key so the server runs again without its cache. The title becomes the AI title once it arrives, and while waiting a spinner shows.
sections.why: Lets a user refresh the AI output on demand while avoiding repeated, costly requests during normal browsing.
sections.watch_out: Because the result is kept indefinitely, old text stays on screen after the data changes until Regenerate is pressed or the project selection changes.

sections.name: SynthesisSlide (part 2)
sections.title: Error, setup notice and result columns
sections.what: Shows an error card with the message and a Retry button when the request fails. Shows a notice to add the AI key secrets when AI is not set up. When the result arrives, shows the two columns, with a plain sentence in each column when it has no items.
sections.why: Each state tells the reader what happened, so an empty or failed slide never looks like a blank page.
sections.watch_out: The setup notice names specific secret names, so it goes stale if the setup changes.

sections.name: SynthesisSlide (part 3)
sections.title: Editorial note, straplines and idle state
sections.what: Adds a small note saying titles, category headers and straplines are AI editorial summaries without claim-level sources. Places the two straplines under the columns. Shows Preparing synthesis while nothing has loaded yet, and closes the citation drawer.
sections.why: Keeps the reader clear about which text is editorial and which is sourced.
sections.watch_out: The note is fixed wording and does not change based on whether sources actually exist.

summary: Slide that shows an AI-written summary of what went wrong and what went right across the selected projects, with a source button next to each claim.
purpose: Gives a reader a themed overview of the selected projects while marking which statements have a source and which do not.
why: The comments say the AI works under a strict no-fabrication rule. The slide shows unsupported claims openly instead of hiding them.
how: 1. Collects the selected projects and their ids. 2. Asks the server for the synthesis, reusing a saved copy unless Regenerate is pressed. 3. Shows a spinner while waiting. 4. Shows an error with Retry, a notice that AI is not set up, or two columns of themed bullets. 5. Each bullet has a source button or is marked unsupported. 6. Ends with two straplines and a note that titles and headers are editorial summaries.
inputs: The selected projects, the industry name and slug, and the page number from the slide context. The server answer from the synthesis request, which says whether a saved copy was used.
outputs: A slide with a title, two columns (what went wrong and what went right), a source button on each bullet, a Regenerate button, and status notes.
risks: Saved copies never expire in the browser, so a changed dataset can show old text until Regenerate is pressed. Claims without sources still look authoritative to a reader who skips the marks. Bullets are matched to projects by name, so a renamed project loses its evidence check. One import sits in the middle of the file, which is easy to miss when editing.
debug: If the slide is blank or stuck, check the synthesis request and response in the browser network tab. If it says not configured, check that the AI key secrets named on the slide are set. If columns look wrong, check the categories in the server response. If source buttons say no src, check that each bullet carries source references. Regenerate forces a fresh server run.
